facts.note: Nine-bell watch check at dinner; narrator's watch exact, doctor's two minutes ahead, Girard would not take his out.
Hall clock struck ten at regulator's 9:48; master's remark about that clock; regulator agreed with the temple bell at ten.
Sent downstairs at regulator's 10:20; regulator was running and master was well; went straight to the kitchen.
That afternoon saw the master in the kitchen with Rosa's clock, laughing; did not ask why.
Looked at Rosa's clock in the kitchen when the piano began (10:58); when piano stopped it showed 11:11.
Stayed in the kitchen with Rosa until after the temple struck eleven.

added.quote: Then the master told each of them what was wrong with theirs.
added.why: Places an event (the master correcting the watches) after the nine o'clock bell, and implies that watches other than the narrator's, including Girard's, were running fast or slow.
